title: Paired Blender 5.2 Material Index owner-identity intervention on the frozen D12.9-H1 temporal candidate
question: When the frozen D12.9-H1 temporal reconstruction receives compiler-assigned Material Index owner tokens instead of Object Index, does the exact same Blender scene/render/candidate matrix eliminate the 15 accepted same-index bilinear owner aliases without introducing any new false accept, quality regression, or nondeterminism?
decisionRole: paired post-hoc causal intervention on the already observed H1 matrix; not a fresh scene holdout and not evidence beyond opaque rigid single-material planar owners

pairedIntervention.unit: the eight H1 fixture/repeat cells and their two rendered frames
frozenFromH1: sceneContract except enabling Material Index pass and assigning material pass indices
all four fixture rasters, cameras, object transforms, object passIndex values, geometry and emission materials
structuralValidity reason order, depth tolerance and fallback
candidateContract Q30/Q24 formula, radius-2 domain, 4x4 support, threshold and reconstruction order
all vector, risk, quality, coverage, disocclusion, stress and static-control thresholds
runtime executables, hashes, OCIO and environment allowlist
onlyAllowedSemanticChange: enable BFS_D129_MASTER.Material Index in addition to the four H1 subimages
assign exactly one compiler token to every analytic owner material
extract previous-owner.f32 and current-owner.f32 from Material Index
retain Object Index as previous-object-index.f32 and current-object-index.f32 negative-control arrays
make the unchanged equality predicates consume Material Index owner arrays
forbidden: changing any H1 RGB, alpha, depth, vector, transform, material signal, Q30/Q24 arithmetic, threshold, mask radius, support footprint, fallback or verdict gate
using analytic owner truth as a consumer decision input
repairing a boundary or fixture-specific mask
changing the 15-pixel primary alias set after observing intervention output
treating fewer accepted pixels alone as success
reusing H1 EXR as intervention render output

materialOwnerTokens.scope: unique within this paired shot/view layer
materialOwnerTokens.compilerInvariant: every material slot visible for one analytic owner must carry the same token; a shared material that would serve different owners must be duplicated before assignment

sourceContract.renderMatrix: four H1 fixtures x two clean repeats x frames 0 and 1 = 16 new Blender 5.2 Cycles CPU renders
sourceContract.materialIndexDomain: finite float32 and every sample is exactly 0 or one declared integer token
sourceContract.objectIndexControl: the H1 object passIndex remains unchanged, including shared 14555 for both SAME_INDEX_DEPTH_CROSSING owners

adapterContract.floatEncoding: little-endian finite float32 with no color transform
adapterContract.overwritePolicy: refuse if output directory or report already exists

h1PayloadIdentity: new previous/current RGBA arrays are byte-identical to the corresponding H1 adapter arrays
new previous/current Depth arrays are byte-identical to H1
new Vector XY/ZW arrays are byte-identical to H1
new Object Index arrays are byte-identical to H1 previous/current owner arrays
pairedIdentityGates.repeatIdentity: all ten canonical arrays, both consumer payload sets and the final decision are byte-identical between R1 and R2 for each fixture
pairedIdentityGates.consumerIdentity: independent Python and Node consumers are byte-identical for reconstructed RGBA, reason, analytic owner, structural, radius, support, accepted and Q30 risk payloads
pairedIdentityGates.independentReplay: the analyzer recomputes the scalar Euler/pinhole/bounded-plane oracle and every frozen H1 decision without importing a consumer

registeredBaseline.definition: H1 accepted.u8 AND NOT C1 true-owner-bilinear.u8; exact coordinate set and count must replay from bound parents

primaryEndpoints.qualityAndFallback: every H1 accepted-quality, risk-underbound, static-control and exact-current fallback threshold remains unchanged
primaryEndpoints.coverage: every H1 coverage threshold remains unchanged and is reported independently; alias elimination cannot excuse a coverage failure

decision.supportedWhen: All identity, runtime, process, source, paired payload, token-domain, projection, structural, primary alias, no-new-accept, safety, risk, quality, fallback, coverage, stress, static-control, attack and audit gates pass.
decision.boundedWhen: All hard identity, primary alias elimination, no-new-accept, safety, quality, fallback, static-control, process, attack and audit gates pass but an unchanged H1 coverage or curvature-stress gate fails.
decision.aliasFailureWhen: Paired identity and hard safety gates pass, but either repeat accepts one or more pixels from the registered 15-pixel alias set or outside true-owner bilinear support.
decision.rejectedWhen: Any parent, freshness, runtime, process, source, paired payload, token-domain, projection, structural, no-new-accept, safety, risk, quality, fallback, static-control, attack or audit-totality gate fails.
decision.noRetroactiveRelabel: No H1, D12.10-C1 or P1-C1 label changes regardless of this outcome.

requirements: tamper any parent, runtime, spec, tool, process, source, adapter, consumer, envelope, result or audit identity
substitute Object Index for Material Index or swap the two channels
reuse a material token, assign zero, exceed 32767, or alter one declared owner token
mutate the critical shared Object Index 14555 negative control
change Combined, Depth, Vector or Object Index while preserving the new owner channel
change a frozen H1 projection, structural, Q30/Q24, threshold, support, coverage, quality, fallback or static-control rule
delete one of the registered 15 alias pixels, alter its coordinate set, or aggregate the two repeats
accept an analytic invalid-history pixel or create any accepted coordinate absent from H1
hide a coverage loss behind alias-elimination success
read current or future RGB while making a temporal decision
The formal and preflight roots and all eight new formal tool paths are absent at preregistration.
This spec is committed and pushed before any new formal tool exists.
Formal output uses 16 new Blender render processes and never copies H1 EXR as source output.
A zero-render preflight may construct every paired scene and inspect RNA but may not create the formal root or write a formal measurement.
The tool freeze commit is later than the preregistration commit and every formal tool byte must match preflight.

runtime.source: exactly inherited from bound H1 spec runtime object

nonClaims: This paired intervention is post-hoc to H1 and does not constitute an unseen-scene holdout.
It does not solve or test the 146/152 one-sided extra-stencil coverage opportunities localized outside the critical same-index fixture.
It tests one material slot per analytic owner and does not yet prove automatic token propagation across multi-material owners or safe duplication of shared materials.
Material Index is limited to integer tokens 0 through 32767 and is not a globally unique asset identifier.
It does not cover curved surfaces, deformation, skinning, transparency, hair, particles, volumes, motion blur, depth of field, noisy lighting or GPU/platform equivalence.
It does not establish perceptual temporal quality, cinematic quality, character consistency, production readiness or a general Blender temporal renderer.
